**Outside trial on main after #392** ([run 43550337827](https://github.com/Expectrail/Expectrail/actions/runs/43550337827), dispatched, no secret, no model spend):

| kinematic-character | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| as pinned | needs-review (the engine passes; vision did not run in CI) |
| broken | **reject**, as expected |
| harmless | needs-review, as expected |

dodge-the-creeps: needs-review, with no ground in any frame.

The engine's record still rejects the real bug, and with no vision key nothing is accepted, as Sean decided on #398. The next step to the first **verified** outside project is one run with vision. No workflow can do that safely yet: the outside game's code must never run in a job that holds the model key. That work is #422.

**First vision run on an outside project** ([run 43559500793](https://github.com/Expectrail/Expectrail/actions/runs/43559500793), the Outside vision workflow from #424, started by Sean; $0.76 at list price, 304 images answered):

| kinematic-character | Verdict | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| as pinned | needs-review | the engine passes; **the vision model found the player in 0 of 120 frames**, so no frame could be judged |
| broken (empty collision mask) | **reject**, as expected | the engine: 71.7 px past the surface at 304.5 from frame 44 |
| harmless (sprite tint) | needs-review, as expected | the same as as-pinned: player found in 0 of 120 frames |

**What this shows, plainly:** the vision model answered every frame, but the default question finds nothing on a game it has never seen. The SAM probe found the same with words on November 12. So no outside project can be verified with vision as it stands, and neither could a customer's game. Every accept on a game that isn't ours would be needs-review. The engine's record still rejects the real bug.

**Next:** this is #330 (tune the visual observer to a game). The architect session takes it as the top priority for the outside path. The approach is to ask the vision model about the place the engine's record puts the player (the probe's anchor mode, and the project config's sprite binding from #259), instead of asking for "a player" in words, and to score that against the engine's record on the clean game before trusting it.
